Glossary

CMS: what is a content management system?

A CMS is software installed behind a website that lets you add or change pages much like filling in a document. The letters stand for Content Management System.

The definition in one sentence

Without a CMS, every change goes through the code, line by line. With a CMS, you log in to an admin interface, type into boxes, add a photo, and click “Publish”.

The CMS stores everything in a database: texts, images, menus, user accounts. It then builds the pages on demand.

What it does for a small business

A CMS keeps a site alive. You can add some news, change your opening hours or post a new project without rebuilding everything. It also lets you add features later: a shop, online booking, a gallery.

The best known are WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, or PrestaShop for selling. There are also online platforms that sell the CMS and the hosting together.

A real-life example

A driving instructor wants to post his new theory course dates every month. With a hand-coded site, he has to call his provider each time. With a CMS, he changes the date in two minutes using a form.

What you need to know

  • A CMS needs looking after. The software and its add-ons get updates, often to close security holes. A CMS that is never updated becomes a target.
  • Freedom comes at a price. The more you can change, the easier it is to break the layout by accident.
  • Time is the real issue. Having a simple tool does not mean having the time to use it in the evening, after work.

Before choosing a CMS, ask yourself who will make the changes. If the answer is “nobody”, even the best tool in the world will stay empty.

Your questions

Do I need a CMS to have a website?

No. A website can be made of simple files, with no database. It is often faster and safer that way. A CMS becomes useful when the content changes often or when several people need to publish.

Which CMS should I choose for my business?

The one that meets your needs and that someone will be able to maintain. For a presentation website or a small shop, the big well-known CMS have the advantage of being well supported, and help is easy to find.
